record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Is there a strongly polynomial-time algorithm for linear programming, meaning an algorithm whose running time does not depend on numerical accuracy parameters and is polynomial only in the combinatorial size of the linear program?

evidence.quote: In principle, such a dependence can be avoided for linear programming and it is a major open problem to find a strongly polynomial algorithm for solving linear programs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A linear program is specified by a matrix $A \in \mathbb{Q}^{m \times n}$, a vector $b \in \mathbb{Q}^m$, and a vector $c \in \mathbb{Q}^n$, and asks to compute $\max\{c^\top x : Ax \le b,\ x \in \mathbb{R}^n\}$ (or report infeasibility/unboundedness). An algorithm in the arithmetic (Blum–Shub–Smale) model of computation is called strongly polynomial if (i) it uses only the elementary arithmetic operations $+,-,\times,\div$ and comparisons on real numbers, charging unit cost per operation; (ii) the total number of such operations is bounded by a polynomial in $m$ and $n$ alone (independent of the bit-sizes or numerical magnitudes of the entries of $A$, $b$, $c$); and (iii) when the input data are rational, the bit-sizes of all numbers occurring during the computation remain polynomially bounded in the bit-size of the input.

Question: Does there exist a strongly polynomial-time algorithm, in the above sense, that solves every linear program?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known major open problem, often listed as Smale's 9th problem for the 21st century. Despite progress on special cases (e.g., LPs with bounded entries by Tardos, Markov decision processes by Ye, and recent work on combinatorial LPs), no strongly polynomial algorithm for general linear programming is known as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Smale's problems - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 9: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm over the real numbers which decides the feasibility of the linear system of inequalities Ax >= b?
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a strongly polynomial LP algorithm is Smale's 9th problem and remains open.

status_evidence.title: Tardos, A strongly polynomial algorithm to solve combinatorial linear programs
status_evidence.snippet: Strongly polynomial algorithms exist for LPs whose constraint matrix has small entries.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases are known to admit strongly polynomial algorithms; the general case is open.
